Engineering

Building an interface without a framework

What you gain, what you give up, and the handful of patterns that make the plain platform pleasant to work in.

AL

Ada Lovelace

6 October 2026 · 8 minute read

The argument for a framework is usually about leverage: someone else has already solved the hard parts, and you get to spend your time on the problem you were actually hired to solve. That argument holds up well. It holds up less well when the hard parts turn out to be ones the platform solved years ago, and the leverage you bought is mostly leverage over your own build configuration.

This page, and the eleven others beside it, are an experiment in going without. One stylesheet, one script, no dependencies beyond two webfonts. What follows is a record of what that cost and what it bought.

What the platform already does

A surprising amount. Modal dialogs, with focus trapping and a backdrop and the top layer, are a single element. Expanding sections are two. Form validation, including the error states and the messages, is a set of attributes. None of these needed a library in the first place; they needed someone to notice they had shipped.

  • dialog — modality, focus, Escape, the backdrop.
  • details and summary — disclosure, searchable by the browser's own find.
  • :has() — styling a parent from its child's state, which removes most of the remaining state classes.
  • Custom properties — real runtime theming, including a dark mode that costs one attribute.

What it costs

Three things, honestly. There is no component model, so repetition is handled by copying markup rather than by composition — which is fine for twelve pages and unpleasant for two hundred. There is no type checking across the boundary between markup and script, so a renamed class fails silently. And there is no ecosystem: a date picker is now your problem.

The platform is not a framework, and pretending otherwise is how you end up writing one badly. — every team that has tried this twice

When it is the right call

Reference sites, documentation, marketing pages, prototypes, and anything that must still work in five years without a dependency audit. The common thread is that the interface is mostly presentational and the interaction is mostly local.

  1. The page count is small enough that duplication stays manageable.
  2. The interactions are local — a menu, a tab set, a dialog — rather than a shared client-side store.
  3. Longevity matters more than iteration speed.

Outside that, reach for the framework. The point was never that frameworks are wasteful; it is that the baseline has moved, and it is worth knowing where to.

Paragraphs

Measure, leading and the first-paragraph lede.

A lede runs one step larger than the body and is muted, which separates it from the article proper without needing a rule or a gap.

Body copy is set at sixteen pixels with a line height of 1.5 and a measure of about sixty-eight characters. That measure is the single most important number on this page: lines much longer than it make the return sweep hard to track, and lines much shorter break the rhythm of reading.

Paragraph spacing comes from the container rather than from margins on the paragraph, so the rhythm holds whatever mix of elements the article turns out to contain.

Wrapping helpers

A balanced heading spreads its words evenly across lines

Pretty wrapping avoids leaving a single short word stranded on the final line of a paragraph, which is otherwise the most common small ugliness in web typography.

Definition list

Token
A named value the whole system reads from, rather than a literal repeated in place.
Role
What a color is for, rather than which color it is — primary, surface, danger.
State layer
A translucent overlay of the foreground color that carries hover, focus and press.
Elevation
How near a surface appears, expressed as a step along the fill ladder rather than as a shadow.
Fill ladder
The four background values — page, surface, raised, hover — that separate one plane from another in place of outlines.

Quotations

Design is not just what it looks like and feels like. Design is how it works. — attributed to Steve Jobs

A short quotation inside a sentence uses the inline element: the platform is not a framework, which the browser renders with the right quotation marks for the document language.

Code

Inline code sits in a tinted pill; blocks sit in a bordered, scrolling well with a copy button that appears on hover.

Call UI.toast() with a message and an options object. Pass duration: 0 to keep it on screen. 

/* Toast with an undo action */
var undo = UI.toast('Conversation archived', {
  action: 'Undo',
  duration: 6000,
  onAction: function () {
    restoreConversation(id);
  }
});

/* Dismiss it early if the view changes underneath */
window.addEventListener('hashchange', undo.dismiss);

Output and samples

Program output uses samp, and something the reader should type uses npm start.

Figures and asides

Supporting material that sits beside the argument rather than inside it.

info
An aside Material that is useful but not load-bearing goes in an aside, which tells assistive technology it can be skipped without losing the thread.

Footnotes

A reference pair of links, so the reader can get down and back.

The state-layer opacities used here are the ones from the original specification[1], with one change: the hover value is doubled in the dark theme, because a four per cent white overlay on a near-black surface is invisible[2].

  1. Four per cent hover, twelve per cent focus, ten per cent pressed. ↩
  2. Eight per cent in dark, sixteen for focus. See the token block at the top of the stylesheet. ↩

Inline elements

The full set, each doing a job no span can do as well.

strong
This is important.
em
This is emphasised.
mark
This is highlighted.
del / ins
Removed text inserted text.
abbr
An CSS abbreviation, with its expansion on hover.
cite
From The Elements of Typographic Style.
time
Published 6 October 2026.
sub / sup
H2O and E = mc2.
small
Fine print and legal notices.
u
A non-textual annotation, such as a spelling error.
s
No longer accurate, but kept for the record.
bdi
User name: إيان — isolated so it cannot reorder the line.
ruby
漢かん字じ — annotation above the base text.
